details: CONFIRMED: reproduced on the trial's own file with the branch's kit. The item's failing case names this F2 and its pass case is
"kit packet --check reports a tasks.md with no Wave line when the tasks run in waves"; every change applied through sdd:parallel-apply
reads the Wave lines (step 1.1), and spec-reviewer rule 12 requires one per group even for the one-task trial change (sequential apply
is a way of running the same groups, and the trial reviewer still asked for "Wave 1 · depends on: none"). So the rule is
unconditional for groups with open tasks; the "some group has one" condition is the fixer's own reading and leaves the trial uncaught.
If the owner wants sequential plans to carry no Wave line, that is a change to spec-reviewer rule 12 and the item stays unfixed;
recorded as inside because the rule already exists. Size: 15 minutes (drop the condition, flip the sequential test, add the trial case).
evidence: spec-1.toml of the trial, F2: summary = "group 1 has no `Wave N · depends on:` line, so apply must plan waves itself"
failing_case: The trial's tasks.md (trial repo commit 3bbf6ce, openspec/changes/add-count-unique-words/tasks.md): one group "## 1. Count distinct
words", one open task, no Wave line anywhere (the reviewer's F2: "group 1 has no `Wave N · depends on:` line"). Branch:
`kit packet --check add-count-unique-words` prints "packet: 1 open task(s), 0 problem(s)", exit 0.
Expected: "group 1: no Wave line ..." and exit 1, as spec-reviewer rule 12 says ("Every group has a `Wave N · depends on:` line").
The new check only fires when some group already has a Wave line (`any(wave_groups.values())`), and the trial author omitted all of
them, so it can never catch the case the item was opened for. test_complete_waves_and_sequential_plans_pass even asserts this
case passes ("No Wave line anywhere ... nothing to check").
fix_hint: In check(): for every group with open tasks, require a `^Wave \d` line in its notes, with no `any(wave_groups.values())` condition;
keep the Wave 1 check (see F2) under "some group has a Wave line other than 0". Change the sequential test to expect exit 1 and
add the trial file's shape as the failing-case test.
pass_cases: - tasks.md "## 1. A" + one open task, no Wave line -> exit 1, output contains "group 1: no Wave line".
- tasks.md "## 1. A\n\nWave 1 · depends on: none" + one open task -> exit 0.
- groups 1 (Wave 0), 2 (no Wave line), 3 (Wave 2), each with an open task -> exit 1, "group 2: no Wave line", not group 1 or 3 (today's test keeps passing).
- groups 1 and 2 with Wave lines whose tasks are all done, group 3 open with a Wave line -> exit 0 (done groups need nothing).
- tasks.md with no open task and no Wave line -> exit 0.
reason: tests/test_fix_reports.py:77 test_no_wave_line_anywhere_is_reported, fails at base, passes; done-group case :84.
findings.summary: the queue item's own failing case still passes: a tasks.md with no Wave line at all is never checked

tasks.md "## 1. A

Wave 0 · depends on: none

- [ ] 1.1 ..." with a valid task -> branch prints "tasks.md: no Wave 1 line: the
